title: 443. Lord Byron: Death of a Vampire (Part 4)

sentences.en: It happened that in the midst of the dissipations attendant upon a London winter, there appeared at the various parties of the leaders of the ton a nobleman,
sentences.zh: 正值伦敦冬日社交狂欢之际，在各界名流的聚会上，出现了一位贵族，

sentences.en: more remarkable for his singularities than his rank.
sentences.zh: 比起他的爵位，他的古怪行径更引人注目。

sentences.en: He gazed upon the mirth around him as if he could not participate therein.
sentences.zh: 他凝视着周围的欢声笑语，仿佛自己无法融入其中。

sentences.en: Apparently, the light laughter of the fair only attracted his attention, that he might by a look quell it and throw fear into those breasts where thoughtlessness reigned.
sentences.zh: 显然，那些佳丽们轻快的笑声之所以能引起他的注意，只是为了让他能用一个眼神将其平息，并给那些本该无忧无虑的心灵带去恐惧。

sentences.en: Those who felt this sensation of awe could not explain whence it arose.
sentences.zh: 那些感受到这种敬畏感的人，却无法解释这种感觉从何而来。

sentences.en: Some attributed it to the dead grey eye, which fixing upon the object's face did not seem to penetrate, and at one glance to pierce through to the inward workings of the heart,
sentences.zh: 有人将其归因于他那死灰般的灰色眼睛，当它盯着某人的脸时，似乎并不只是在注视，而是一眼就能洞穿人心深处的运作，

sentences.en: but fell upon the cheek with a leaden ray that weighed upon the skin it could not pass.
sentences.zh: 而是带着一种铅灰色的光芒落在对方脸颊上，那光芒沉重得仿佛压在皮肤上却无法穿透。

sentences.en: His peculiarities caused him to be invited to every house.
sentences.zh: 他的怪癖使他成了每家每户争相邀请的对象。

sentences.en: All wished to see him, and those who had been accustomed to violent excitement and now felt the weight of ennui
sentences.zh: 所有人都想见他，而那些习惯了强烈刺激、如今正感到百无聊赖的人，

sentences.en: were pleased at having something in their presence capable of engaging their attention, in spite of the deadly hue of his face, which never gained a warmer tint,
sentences.zh: 却很高兴能在身边有这样一个能吸引他们注意力的人，尽管他那张脸有着死一般的惨白，从未泛起过一丝红润，

sentences.en: either from the blush of modesty or from the strong emotion of passion.
sentences.zh: 无论是出于羞涩的红晕，还是出于强烈的激情。

sentences.en: Though its form and outline were beautiful, many of the female hunters after notoriety attempted to win his attentions
sentences.zh: 尽管他的外形和轮廓都很俊美，许多追求名气的女性猎手还是试图赢得他的青睐，

sentences.en: and gain at least some marks of what they might term affection.
sentences.zh: 并至少获得一些她们称之为“爱慕”的表示。

sentences.en: So that, Tom, is the opening of a novel called The Vampire, published in 1819.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这就是1819年出版的小说《吸血鬼》的开篇。

sentences.en: It carried the attribution, a tale by Lord Byron.
sentences.zh: 它署名是“拜伦勋爵著”。

sentences.en: So listeners can be reassured it's not one of your own early works.
sentences.zh: 所以听众们可以放心，这不是你早期的作品之一。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: But it has a really interesting backstory, an interesting history, this book, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这本书确实有一个非常有趣的背景故事，一段有趣的历史，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because it's not by Lord Byron.
sentences.zh: 因为它并不是拜伦勋爵写的。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: It's not.
sentences.zh: 确实不是。

sentences.en: Although you can completely see, listening to that, why people would think that it was by Byron, because it's patently modelled on Byron's years of fame in London.
sentences.zh: 虽然听了刚才那段，你完全能理解为什么人们会认为它是拜伦写的，因为它显然是以拜伦在伦敦成名那几年的生活为蓝本的。

sentences.en: There's a reference to a Lady Mercer who dresses up as a mountebank and throws herself in this aristocrat's way.
sentences.zh: 书中提到了一个叫默瑟夫人的角色，她打扮成江湖郎中，主动投怀送抱。

sentences.en: And that's clearly modelled on Caroline Lamb.
sentences.zh: 这显然是以卡罗琳·兰姆为原型。

sentences.en: And what makes that absolutely certain is that the fact that the name of this mysterious lord,
sentences.zh: 而最能确凿证明这一点的是，这位神秘勋爵的名字，

sentences.en: Lord Ruffin, derived from a novel that Caroline Lamb had written, in which the hero is called Lord Ruffin and is clearly Lord Byron.
sentences.zh: 鲁芬勋爵，源自卡罗琳·兰姆写的一部小说，书中的男主角就叫鲁芬勋爵，而且显然就是拜伦勋爵本人。

sentences.en: And what makes this all the more intriguing is that Lord Ruffin is a vampire.
sentences.zh: 更耐人寻味的是，这位鲁芬勋爵是个吸血鬼。

sentences.en: And in fact, he is the first aristocratic vampire, because until this point, vampires was a kind of Balkan peasant superstition.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他是第一位贵族吸血鬼，因为在此之前，吸血鬼只是一种巴尔干半岛的农民迷信。

sentences.en: And Byron had learnt about it in the Balkans, as we will see in due course.
sentences.zh: 正如我们稍后会看到的，拜伦是在巴尔干半岛了解到这一点的。

sentences.en: And so when this book gets published, it's widely interpreted as a kind of a confession, an acknowledgement by Byron that he was indeed guilty of all the terrible sins
sentences.zh: 所以当这本书出版时，它被广泛解读为一种忏悔，一种拜伦的自我承认，承认他确实犯下了所有那些

sentences.en: that people think that he's guilty of.
sentences.zh: 人们认为他犯下的可怕罪行。

sentences.en: And we left him at the end of the previous episode going into exile and this shadow of the satanic hanging over him.
sentences.zh: 上一集结束时，我们讲到他流亡海外，而撒旦般的阴影笼罩着他。

sentences.en: And so people read this book and think, yeah, okay, this is, you know, he's basically fessing up.
sentences.zh: 所以人们读到这本书时会想，没错，好吧，他基本上是在坦白。

sentences.en: But as you say, it's not actually by Byron.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，它实际上并不是拜伦写的。

sentences.en: So just before you say who it is by, Tom, just to recap, we left Byron at the end of the last episode.
sentences.zh: 所以在你揭晓作者是谁之前，汤姆，我们先回顾一下上一集结尾拜伦的情况。

sentences.en: We did the first episode all about his upbringing.
sentences.zh: 我们讲了第一集，全是关于他的成长经历。

sentences.en: Then we had his great travels, meeting with the Sultan, Ali Pasha, falling in love with Greece, being crossed with Lord Elgin.
sentences.zh: 然后是他伟大的旅行，会见苏丹、阿里帕夏，爱上希腊，与埃尔金勋爵发生冲突。

sentences.en: And then the last episode, this absolutely bizarre, dangerous liaison-style love life that he has back in England.
sentences.zh: 接着是上一集，他在英国那段绝对离奇、危险的“危险关系”式的爱情生活。

sentences.en: There are accusations of incest and sodomy in the air, and he has fled England forever into exile.
sentences.zh: 当时空气中弥漫着乱伦和鸡奸的指控，他永远地逃离了英国，开始了流亡生涯。

sentences.en: And as you say, the vampirism, I mean, that's basically a sort of a metaphor, isn't it, for the sexual misconduct with which he's been charged.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，吸血鬼这个意象，基本上就是他所受到的性丑闻指控的一种隐喻，不是吗？

sentences.en: Not charged sort of publicly, but charged in the sort of salons and in the gossip of aristocratic London.
sentences.zh: 不是公开指控，而是在伦敦贵族沙龙和流言蜚语中的指控。

sentences.en: I mean, he remains complete box office.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他依然是绝对的票房保证。

sentences.en: And so the measure of this is that he's hired a physician, a young English doctor of Italian extraction called John Polidori to go with him.
sentences.zh: 所以衡量这一点的方法是，他雇了一位医生，一位有意大利血统的年轻英国医生约翰·波利多里随行。

sentences.en: And John Murray, who is Byron's publisher, is paying him a fortune to write a journal of what happens.
sentences.zh: 而拜伦的出版商约翰·默里付给他一大笔钱，让他记录下发生的一切。

sentences.en: And it's Polidori who actually has written this account when it comes out in 1819.
sentences.zh: 而当1819年这本书出版时，正是波利多里写下了这份记录。

sentences.en: And Polidori has a very awkward relationship with Byron because he, as well as being a doctor, he's an ambitious writer.
sentences.zh: 波利多里与拜伦的关系非常尴尬，因为他不仅是一名医生，还是一位雄心勃勃的作家。

sentences.en: And he's actually written three tragedies.
sentences.zh: 他实际上写了三部悲剧。

sentences.en: And before they leave Dover for Ostend, he reads one of these tragedies out to Byron and Hobhouse, and both of them fall about laughing.
sentences.zh: 在他们离开多佛前往奥斯坦德之前，他把其中一部悲剧读给拜伦和霍布豪斯听，结果两人都笑得前仰后合。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's very, very difficult.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这非常非常尴尬。

sentences.en: But Polidori knows the kind of details that his readership will want.
sentences.zh: 但波利多里知道他的读者想要什么样的细节。

sentences.en: So his description of Byron's arrival in Ghent after they've landed is very famous.
sentences.zh: 所以他关于拜伦登陆后抵达根特的描述非常出名。

sentences.en: As soon as he reached his room, Polidori wrote,
sentences.zh: 波利多里写道，他一到房间，

sentences.en: Lord Byron fell like a thunderbolt upon the chambermaid.
sentences.zh: 拜伦勋爵就像一道闪电般扑向了女仆。

sentences.en: And did he?
sentences.zh: 他真的这么做了吗？

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: And also, of course, what we don't know is whether the chambermaid is willing or not.
sentences.zh: 而且当然，我们也不知道那个女仆是否自愿。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是啊，当然。

sentences.en: There's all kinds of things being unspoken there.
sentences.zh: 那里有很多未言明的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, probably she was.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她很可能是自愿的。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, Byron is the most famous and handsome man in the world.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，拜伦是世界上最出名、最英俊的男人。

sentences.en: But as they're going, Byron too is writing, and he is returning to Childe Harold's pilgrimage.
sentences.zh: 但当他们赶路时，拜伦也在写作，他正在回归《恰尔德·哈罗德游记》。

sentences.en: And so essentially, as he travels through Europe and he's heading southwards, he never visits France, interestingly, but he goes down the Rhine towards Switzerland
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，当他穿过欧洲向南行进时，有趣的是他从未访问过法国，但他沿着莱茵河向瑞士走去，

sentences.en: in kind of very modest way that is typical of him.
sentences.zh: 以一种他特有的、非常低调的方式。

sentences.en: He is aligning all the agonies and the dramas of recent history with his own.
sentences.zh: 他将近代史上所有的痛苦和戏剧性与他自己的经历联系在一起。

sentences.en: So he visits the battlefield of Waterloo.
sentences.zh: 所以他参观了滑铁卢战场。

sentences.en: He tours it.
sentences.zh: 他游览了那里。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's this famous ball before the Battle of Waterloo held by the Duchess of Richmond.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，里士满公爵夫人在滑铁卢战役前举办了那场著名的舞会。

sentences.en: And Byron famously writes about it in Childe Harold.
sentences.zh: 拜伦在《恰尔德·哈罗德游记》中著名地写到了它。

sentences.en: And he is essentially comparing the agonies of those at the ball to his own agonies.
sentences.zh: 他本质上是在将舞会上人们的痛苦与他自己的痛苦进行比较。

sentences.en: So he writes, there was a sound of revelry by night and Belgium's capital had gathered then her beauty and her chivalry and bright the lamps shone over fair women and brave men.
sentences.zh: 所以他写道：夜色中传来狂欢之声，比利时的首都聚集了她的佳丽与骑士，灯火辉煌，照耀着美丽的女人和勇敢的男人。

sentences.en: A thousand hearts beat happily.
sentences.zh: 千颗心快乐地跳动着。

sentences.en: And when music arose with its voluptuous swell, soft eyes looked love to eyes which spake again and all went merry as a marriage bell.
sentences.zh: 当音乐响起，带着撩人的旋律，温柔的眼睛向眼睛诉说着爱意，一切都像婚礼的钟声一样欢快。

sentences.en: But hush, hark, a deep sound strikes like a rising knell.
sentences.zh: 但嘘，听，一声沉重的轰鸣，宛如丧钟响起。

sentences.en: So this is the onset of war, of the Battle of Waterloo.
sentences.zh: 所以这是战争的开始，滑铁卢战役的开始。

sentences.en: But it's also the doom that will torpedo Byron's reputation as the social lion of London.
sentences.zh: 但这也是将摧毁拜伦作为伦敦社交界宠儿声誉的厄运。

sentences.en: And you may wonder, you know, how can he get away with this?
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，他怎么能逃脱惩罚呢？

sentences.en: No matter how famous he is, how can someone conceivably compare his kind of marital agonies with all the dead of Waterloo?
sentences.zh: 无论他有多出名，一个人怎么能把自己的婚姻痛苦与滑铁卢的所有死者相提并论？

sentences.en: And I think it is precisely because with Napoleon now gone into exile, Byron is the most celebrated person in Europe and he is an object of consuming curiosity wherever he goes.
sentences.zh: 我认为这恰恰是因为随着拿破仑流亡，拜伦成了欧洲最著名的人，无论他走到哪里，他都是人们极度好奇的对象。

sentences.en: Tom, we talked before about, I mentioned Stendhal's novel, The Rouge et le Noir.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们之前谈到过，我提到了司汤达的小说《红与黑》。

sentences.en: Stendhal who met Byron, great French writer.
sentences.zh: 司汤达见过拜伦，伟大的法国作家。

sentences.en: And that novel captures this sort of adolescent hero worship of Napoleon by people who are seized with a kind of yearning to lift themselves out of provincial mediocrity.
sentences.zh: 那部小说捕捉到了那种青少年对拿破仑的崇拜，这些人渴望摆脱平庸的省城生活。

sentences.en: You know, they worship Napoleon.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们崇拜拿破仑。

sentences.en: Napoleon made himself a great man.
sentences.zh: 拿破仑成就了伟大的自我。

sentences.en: He's above the common herd.
sentences.zh: 他凌驾于芸芸众生之上。

sentences.en: Obviously, that impulse lies at the heart of romanticism, of the idea of the romantic artiSt.
sentences.zh: 显然，这种冲动是浪漫主义的核心，是浪漫主义艺术家理念的核心。

sentences.en: It's why people admire our old friend John Lennon.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们钦佩我们的老朋友约翰·列侬。

sentences.en: They think he's better than the norm.
sentences.zh: 他们认为他比普通人更好。

sentences.en: You know, he's different.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他与众不同。

sentences.en: He's a suffering artiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一位痛苦的艺术家。

sentences.en: He's special.
sentences.zh: 他是特别的。

sentences.en: Do you think the same people who idolize Napoleon idolize Byron?
sentences.zh: 你认为那些崇拜拿破仑的人也崇拜拜伦吗？

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全是这样。

sentences.en: And I think more than that.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为不仅如此。

sentences.en: I think that when they idolize Napoleon, Byron serves as a filter for them.
sentences.zh: 我认为当他们崇拜拿破仑时，拜伦充当了他们的过滤器。

sentences.en: So it does for Stendhal.
sentences.zh: 对司汤达来说就是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, Stendhal admires Napoleon, but he also admires Byron.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，司汤达钦佩拿破仑，但也钦佩拜伦。

sentences.en: And the two are conflated.
sentences.zh: 两者被混为一谈了。

sentences.en: And actually, particularly in France, interestingly.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，特别是在法国，这很有趣。

sentences.en: So Byron is hugely influenced on the course that French romanticism takes.
sentences.zh: 所以拜伦对法国浪漫主义的发展方向产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: So it's not just an English thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是英国的事情。

sentences.en: Okay, interesting.
sentences.zh: 好吧，很有趣。

sentences.en: And that means that when he turns up in Switzerland, for instance, you know, he is as obsessive a topic of interest to the Swiss as to English tourists there.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当他出现在瑞士时，你知道，他成了瑞士人眼中和当地英国游客眼中同样令人痴迷的话题。

sentences.en: And wherever he goes, people are kind of watching him, pointing at him.
sentences.zh: 无论他走到哪里，人们都在盯着他，对他指指点点。

sentences.en: Byron reports that, you know, he walks into a room and a woman faints.
sentences.zh: 拜伦报告说，他走进一个房间，一位女士晕倒了。

sentences.en: And he says, well, it's a bit, you know, it's a bit much.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，这有点，你知道，这有点过分了。

sentences.en: And kind of entrepreneurial Swiss hoteliers are hiring out binoculars that they can spy on him.
sentences.zh: 而那些精明的瑞士酒店老板甚至出租望远镜，好让他们偷窥他。

sentences.en: So it's awful.
sentences.zh: 所以这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And it's not surprising that when Byron, he arrives at the Hotel d'Angleterre in Geneva, you know, he's asked to give his name and his age.
sentences.zh: 难怪当拜伦抵达日内瓦的英格兰酒店时，他被要求写下姓名和年龄。

sentences.en: And he writes down, I am a hundred.
sentences.zh: 他写道：我一百岁了。

sentences.en: You know, he's feeling exhausted by everything.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他感到精疲力竭。

sentences.en: And so it's not surprising, therefore, that he is in a mood to welcome interesting and convivial company.
sentences.zh: 所以难怪他现在的心情很想迎接有趣且友好的陪伴。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The company of people who will not cause him grief.
sentences.zh: 陪伴那些不会给他带来痛苦的人。

sentences.en: And on the 27th of May, 1816, he and Polidori have been out on a boat on Lake Geneva.
sentences.zh: 1816年5月27日，他和波利多里在日内瓦湖上划船回来。

sentences.en: And they come back and they get onto the jetty.
sentences.zh: 他们回到码头上。

sentences.en: And there on the jetty, a young man and two women are waiting for him.
sentences.zh: 码头上，一个年轻人和两个女人正在等他。

sentences.en: And this is one of the famous meetings in literary history.
sentences.zh: 这是文学史上著名的会面之一。

sentences.en: Because, of course, that young man is the 23-year-old Percy Bysshe Shelley, who, like Byron, is a poet.
sentences.zh: 因为那个年轻人当然就是23岁的珀西·比希·雪莱，他像拜伦一样也是位诗人。

sentences.en: You know, he's not published and famous in the way that Byron is.
sentences.zh: 他不像拜伦那样出名且作品广为人知。

sentences.en: But he kind of pushes sceptical trends that Byron has to very radical limits.
sentences.zh: 但他把拜伦所持的怀疑论推向了非常激进的极限。

sentences.en: So he's an open atheist, an open Republican, an enthusiast for free love.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个公开的无神论者、公开的共和主义者，也是自由恋爱的狂热支持者。

sentences.en: And he has with him two stepsisters.
sentences.zh: 他带着两个继姐妹。

sentences.en: So one of them, Mary Godwin, who in due course will become Mary Shelley, is the daughter of two very famous parents.
sentences.zh: 其中一个，玛丽·戈德温，后来成为了玛丽·雪莱，是两位非常著名父母的女儿。

sentences.en: So William Godwin is a kind of radical, sceptical philosopher.
sentences.zh: 威廉·戈德温是一位激进的怀疑论哲学家。

sentences.en: And her mother, Mary Wollstonecraft, is pioneering feminiSt.
sentences.zh: 她的母亲玛丽·沃斯通克拉夫特是先驱女权主义者。

sentences.en: And she is sleeping with Shelley.
sentences.zh: 她当时正和雪莱同居。

sentences.en: And with her is her stepsister, who's younger than her, Claire Claremont.
sentences.zh: 和她在一起的还有她比她年轻的继姐妹，克莱尔·克莱蒙特。

sentences.en: And the meeting between Shelley and the two stepsisters with Byron is initially awkward.
sentences.zh: 雪莱和两个继姐妹与拜伦的初次见面很尴尬。

sentences.en: This is partly because Polidori actually is very saturnine, very good looking.
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为波利多里其实长得很阴郁、很帅气。

sentences.en: And Shelley mistakes Polidori for Byron.
sentences.zh: 雪莱误把波利多里当成了拜伦。

sentences.en: Oh, my word.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So that slightly deflates Byron's image.
sentences.zh: 这稍微削弱了拜伦的形象。

sentences.en: It does, slightly.
sentences.zh: 确实，稍微有一点。

sentences.en: He can be mistaken for him.
sentences.zh: 他竟然会被人认错。

sentences.en: It's also the fact both men are naturally shy.
sentences.zh: 这也是因为两人天生都很害羞。

sentences.en: So it takes some time for their reserve to break down.
sentences.zh: 所以他们花了些时间才打破隔阂。

sentences.en: And it's also because there is a massive fly in the ointment.
sentences.zh: 而且还有一个巨大的麻烦。

sentences.en: And that is that Claire Claremont has not only slept with Byron, but got pregnant by him.
sentences.zh: 那就是克莱尔·克莱蒙特不仅和拜伦睡过，还怀了他的孩子。

sentences.en: And so she had set out to seduce him while he was in the kind of the depths of misery.
sentences.zh: 所以她在拜伦处于极度痛苦时主动去诱惑他。

sentences.en: His wife had left him.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子离开了他。

sentences.en: He's being abused across London.
sentences.zh: 他在伦敦到处受辱。

sentences.en: And so he basically succumbs to her advances.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上屈服于她的追求。

sentences.en: He'd been upfront right from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 他从一开始就直言不讳。

sentences.en: I'm not interested in a relationship.
sentences.zh: 我对恋爱没兴趣。

sentences.en: I'll do this because you're kind of pestering me.
sentences.zh: 我会这么做是因为你一直在纠缠我。

sentences.en: But I don't want anything more to do with you.
sentences.zh: 但我不想再和你有什么瓜葛了。

sentences.en: So his comment on it was, I never loved nor pretended to love her.
sentences.zh: 所以他对此的评论是：我从未爱过她，也从未假装爱过她。

sentences.en: But a man is a man.
sentences.zh: 但男人毕竟是男人。

sentences.en: And if a girl of 18, in fact, she's 17, comes prancing to you at all hours, there is but one way.
sentences.zh: 如果一个18岁的女孩——其实她才17岁——在任何时候都对你投怀送抱，那只有一个办法。

sentences.en: And so Claire, a bit like Caroline Lamb, is obsessed with him, is pursuing him.
sentences.zh: 所以克莱尔，有点像卡罗琳·兰姆，对他着了迷，一直在追求他。

sentences.en: But to be fair, she's pregnant by him.
sentences.zh: 但平心而论，她怀了他的孩子。

sentences.en: I mean, it's understandable that she would be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她会这样也是可以理解的。

sentences.en: Yeah, she is.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: And she's persuaded Shelley and Mary, basically, to go to Geneva so that they can meet with Byron.
sentences.zh: 她基本上说服了雪莱和玛丽去日内瓦，这样他们就能见到拜伦了。

sentences.en: So despite the awkwardness of this beginning, Byron and Shelley get on well.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管开头有些尴尬，拜伦和雪莱还是相处得很好。

sentences.en: And as I'm sure most listeners will know, because this is very, very celebrated, the two poets, the two stepsisters, Polidori, they essentially spend that summer together.
sentences.zh: 我相信大多数听众都知道，因为这件事非常非常出名，两位诗人、两位继姐妹和波利多里，他们基本上一起度过了那个夏天。

sentences.en: So the Shelley's hire a small house beside Lake Geneva, and Byron rents a villa, the Villa
sentences.zh: 雪莱夫妇在日内瓦湖畔租了一栋小房子，而拜伦租了一栋别墅，即迪奥达蒂别墅，

sentences.en: Diodati, where John Milton, the great poet, had once stayed, which is above Shelley's villa, kind of spectacular views over the lake towards the Dura Mountains.
sentences.zh: 伟大的诗人约翰·弥尔顿曾经住过那里，它位于雪莱别墅的上方，可以欣赏到湖泊向汝拉山脉延伸的壮丽景色。

sentences.en: And they go on tours around the neighbouring sites.
sentences.zh: 他们还去周边的景点游览。

sentences.en: But they are kept in by what is famously terrible weather.
sentences.zh: 但因为众所周知的糟糕天气，他们被困在了室内。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's the year without a summer.
sentences.zh: 没错，那是“无夏之年”。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's been this volcano that has erupted in Indonesia the year before, and the ash has basically blotted out the sun.
sentences.zh: 前一年印度尼西亚的一座火山爆发了，火山灰基本上遮住了太阳。

sentences.en: And Dominic, it's this.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，就是这个。

sentences.en: You've done a series, haven't you, on Frankenstein and science fiction?
sentences.zh: 你不是做过一个关于《弗兰肯斯坦》和科幻小说的系列节目吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, TV series.
sentences.zh: 是的，电视系列节目。

sentences.en: Yeah, years ago, years ago.
sentences.zh: 没错，那是几年前的事了，好几年前了。

sentences.en: So they have the famous competition, don't they?
sentences.zh: 所以他们举行了那场著名的比赛，对吧？

sentences.en: Write a ghost story.
sentences.zh: 写一个鬼故事。

sentences.en: It's actually a Doctor Who story about this, Tom, where they've got a cyber man in the cellar, but we don't need to get into that now.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这其实是一个《神秘博士》的故事，他们在地窖里关了一个赛博人，但我们现在不需要讨论这个。

sentences.en: They don't go into that.
sentences.zh: 他们没谈那个。

sentences.en: They're all sort of trying to scare each other with different stories, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 他们都在试图用不同的故事吓唬对方，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so Polidori gives an account of it, and at 12 o'clock, really began to talk ghostly.
sentences.zh: 是的，波利多里对此有记录，说在12点的时候，他们真的开始谈论鬼怪了。

sentences.en: Elby, so that's Byron, repeated some verses of Coleridge's Christabel of the Witch's BreaSt.
sentences.zh: 埃尔比，也就是拜伦，背诵了柯勒律治《克里斯塔贝尔》中关于女巫乳房的一些诗句。

sentences.en: When silence ensued, Shelley, suddenly shrieking and putting his hands to his head, ran out of the room with a candle.
sentences.zh: 当沉默降临时，雪莱突然尖叫起来，双手抱头，拿着蜡烛跑出了房间。

sentences.en: He was looking at Mrs. Shelley and suddenly thought of a woman he had heard of who had eyes instead of nipples, which, taking hold of his mind, horrified him.
sentences.zh: 他当时正看着雪莱夫人，突然想起了他听说过的一个女人，那个女人的乳头位置长着眼睛，这占据了他的脑海，让他感到恐惧。

sentences.en: To be fair, that would freak you out.
sentences.zh: 说实话，那确实会把你吓坏。

sentences.en: I mean, that is...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那真是……

sentences.en: Yeah, it would, wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 没错，会吓坏的，不是吗？

sentences.en: It absolutely would.
sentences.zh: 绝对会。

sentences.en: But especially, I mean, if I was Mrs. Shelley, I would be quite offended by that.
sentences.zh: 但特别是，如果我是雪莱夫人，我会对此感到相当被冒犯。

sentences.en: Well, there's the Ken Russell film, Gothic.
sentences.zh: 嗯，肯·罗素拍过一部电影叫《哥特》。

sentences.en: Right, I've never seen that.
sentences.zh: 对，我没看过那部。

sentences.en: Which brings all that to life.
sentences.zh: 那部电影把这一切都演活了。

sentences.en: So this ghost story competition, Shelley gets bored.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个鬼故事比赛中，雪莱感到无聊了。

sentences.en: Polidori's story is terrible, but there are two hugely influential stories that do emerge from it.
sentences.zh: 波利多里的故事很糟糕，但确实从中诞生了两个影响深远的故事。

sentences.en: And the most famous of these, of course, is Frankenstein.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中最著名的是《弗兰肯斯坦》。

sentences.en: And we will be doing an episode specifically on Frankenstein.
sentences.zh: 我们将专门做一期关于《弗兰肯斯坦》的节目。

sentences.en: We will.
sentences.zh: 我们会做的。

sentences.en: We'll do a separate episode on Frankenstein, because it's such a brilliant story.
sentences.zh: 我们会单独做一期关于《弗兰肯斯坦》的节目，因为它是一个如此精彩的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah, so we'll just park that.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们就先搁置一下。

sentences.en: But Byron tells a story which is clearly very autobiographical about an aristocrat who comes from the Balkans to London and turns out to be a vampire.
sentences.zh: 但拜伦讲了一个故事，显然带有很强的自传色彩，讲的是一个贵族从巴尔干半岛来到伦敦，结果发现是个吸血鬼。

sentences.en: And as I said, he's drawing on superstitions that he had heard in Greece and Albania.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，他借鉴了他在希腊和阿尔巴尼亚听到的迷信传说。

sentences.en: And he wrote a poem called The Jawa, in which a curse is delivered on the eponymous Jawa.
sentences.zh: 他写了一首名为《异教徒》的诗，其中对同名的异教徒下了诅咒。

sentences.en: The Jawa is a Turkish word for a kind of a frank, a westerner.
sentences.zh: “异教徒”是一个土耳其语词汇，指一种法兰克人，即西方人。

sentences.en: And this is the curse.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个诅咒。

sentences.en: Thy course shall from its tomb be rent, then ghastly haunt thy native place, and suck the blood of all thy race.
sentences.zh: 你的尸体将从坟墓中被撕裂，然后阴森地萦绕在你的故土，吸干你所有族人的鲜血。

sentences.en: There from thy daughter, sister, wife, at midnight drain the stream of life.
sentences.zh: 在那里，从你的女儿、姐妹、妻子身上，在午夜吸干生命的源泉。

sentences.en: Yet loathe the banquet which perforce must feed thy livid living course.
sentences.zh: 然而却厌恶那场不得不喂养你那青紫活尸的盛宴。

sentences.en: Thy victims, ere they yet expire, shall know the demon for their sire.
sentences.zh: 你的受害者，在他们断气之前，就会认出这个恶魔就是他们的父亲。

sentences.en: As cursing thee, thou cursing them, thy flowers are withered on the stem.
sentences.zh: 正如诅咒你一样，你也在诅咒他们，你的花朵在茎上枯萎。

sentences.en: And what is interesting about that, we talked in the previous episode about Lady Byron going
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我们在上一集谈到拜伦夫人去找她的医生，说拜伦有一种想法，认为自己被诅咒了，要摧毁所有爱他和他所爱的人。

sentences.en: to her doctor and saying that Byron has this idea that he is cursed to destroy all those who love him and who he loves.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，其中确实有这些成分。

sentences.en: I mean, there's elements of that.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 女儿、姐妹、妻子。

sentences.en: Thy daughter, sister, wife.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来像是拜伦床上的那些人。

sentences.en: I mean, that sounds like the inhabitants of Byron's bed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，但那种认为性和性欲在某种程度上是有毒且被玷污的想法，你可以看出它来自哪里，我的意思是，这甚至不是他的潜意识，而是他的意识。

sentences.en: I mean, but the idea of sexuality and sexual desire being poisonous in some way and being
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: tainted, you can see why that comes from, I mean, it's barely even his subconscious, it's his consciousness.
sentences.zh: 而且你绝对能明白为什么后来波利多里以拜伦的名义发表作品时，每个人都认为那是拜伦写的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 也明白为什么那种既美丽又致命的贵族吸血鬼形象会变得如此有影响力。

sentences.en: And you can absolutely see why in due cause Polidori publishes under Byron's name, why everyone assumes that it is by Byron.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，如果没有以拜伦勋爵为原型的罗斯福勋爵，就不会有德古拉伯爵。

sentences.en: And also why that image of the aristocratic vampire, who is beautiful as well as deadly, becomes so influential.
sentences.zh: 你指出了这一点，对吧，以前的吸血鬼都是从巴尔干半岛那些蚊虫叮咬的村庄坟墓里爬出来的农民形象。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, you wouldn't have Count Dracula without Lord Rothfuss, who is based on Lord Byron.
sentences.zh: 肮脏的。

sentences.en: You make the point, don't you, that previously vampires had been peasant figures climbing out of sort of graves in fly-bitten Balkan villages.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Dirty.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 那种风度翩翩的想法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 德古拉伯爵太有拜伦风格了。

sentences.en: The idea of the suave.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，想想弗朗西斯·福特·科波拉的电影。

sentences.en: Count Dracula is so Byronic.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: I mean, think of Francis Ford Coppola's film.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切，你知道，和雪莱一家混在一起。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些都无助于改善拜伦的名声，因为雪莱臭名昭著。

sentences.en: So all of this, you know, the hanging out with the Shelleys.
sentences.zh: 人们认为他同时和那两个姐妹，也就是继姐妹睡觉，但她们被说成是姐妹。

sentences.en: I mean, none of this does anything to improve Byron's reputation because Shelly is notorious.
sentences.zh: 所以回到伦敦，传言会说拜伦和雪莱陷入了乱伦的勾当。

sentences.en: People think that he's sleeping with both the sisters, the stepsisters, but they're kind of, you know, they're talked of as being sisters.
sentences.zh: 这正好利用了拜伦自己的名声。

sentences.en: And so back in London, the rumours will be that Byron and Shelly are engaged in a league of inceSt.
sentences.zh: 拜伦听到这些传闻时非常愤怒，因为事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And so that's making play with Byron's own reputation.
sentences.zh: 雪莱并没有同时和克莱尔以及玛丽睡觉。

sentences.en: Byron, when he hears about this, is furious because actually it's not true.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为更重要的是，拜伦在这些事件中的表现相当糟糕。

sentences.en: Shelly isn't sleeping with Claire as well as with Mary.
sentences.zh: 例如，他在对待自由恋爱等态度上不如雪莱激进。

sentences.en: And also, I think what is more is that Byron's been behaving quite badly in these episodes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可能会让听过上一集的听众感到惊讶，但雪莱在观点上确实相当激进。

sentences.en: He is less radical than Shelly in his attitudes, for instance, towards free love.
sentences.zh: 而且雪莱也有能力发现拜伦令人震惊的一面，不仅是震惊，而且我认为他也被拜伦吓到了，既因为他是勋爵，也因为他的名气。

sentences.en: I mean, that may come as a surprise to listeners to the previous episode, but Shelly really is kind of radical in his views.
sentences.zh: 当然，拜伦仍然拒绝与克莱尔有任何瓜葛，这又投下了一层阴影。

sentences.en: And Shelly also is capable of finding Byron shocking and not only shocking, but also is quite intimidated by him, I think, both because he's a lord, but also because of his fame.
sentences.zh: 所以雪莱一家在与拜伦共处三个月后，于8月29日离开了日内瓦，他们讨论了克莱尔的孩子将来出生后的去向。

sentences.en: And of course, a further shadow is cast by the fact that Byron is still refusing to have anything to do with Claire.
sentences.zh: 拜伦提议让奥古斯塔抚养这个孩子。

sentences.en: And so the Shelleys leave Geneva on the 29th of August after their three month stay with
sentences.zh: 雪莱说，绝对不行。

sentences.en: Byron, and they discuss the future of Claire's child when she, in due course, gives birth to it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就是他一直与之发生关系的那个姐妹。

sentences.en: Byron proposes that Augusta should raise it.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Shelly's saying, absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，拜托。

sentences.en: Well, his sister that he's been sleeping with.
sentences.zh: 那太荒谬了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 最终达成一致，孩子出生后将由父母中的一方抚养。

sentences.en: I mean, come on.
sentences.zh: 拜伦勉强同意了这一点。

sentences.en: That's ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 克莱尔走了，拜伦没有和她告别，也没有拥抱她。

sentences.en: It's finally agreed that the child, when he or she is born, will live with either one of the parents.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他不想和她有任何瓜葛。

sentences.en: And Byron reluctantly agrees with this.
sentences.zh: 所以雪莱一家回到英国，1817年1月中旬，克莱尔临产，生下了一个女儿。

sentences.en: Claire goes, Byron does not say goodbye to her, does not embrace her.
sentences.zh: 所以这是拜伦的第二个女儿。

sentences.en: You know, he doesn't want to have anything to do with her.
sentences.zh: 雪莱一家叫她阿尔芭，这是他们根据阿尔巴尼亚给拜伦起的昵称。

sentences.en: So the Shelleys go back to England and mid-January, 1817, Claire goes into labour, gives birth, and it's a daughter.
sentences.zh: 所以他们叫这个女孩阿尔芭。

sentences.en: So Byron's second daughter.
sentences.zh: 但拜伦坚持要叫她阿莱格拉。

sentences.en: And the Shelleys call her Alba, which had been their pet name for Byron after Albania.
sentences.zh: 他这样做的原因是，到1817年冬天，他已经从瑞士翻越了阿尔卑斯山。

sentences.en: And so they called this girl Alba.
sentences.zh: 他穿过了意大利北部，最终到达了威尼斯。

sentences.en: But Byron insists that they call her Allegra.
sentences.zh: 而阿莱格拉是一个威尼斯名字。

sentences.en: And the reason that he does that is that by this point in the winter of 1817, he's crossed the Alps from Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 当珀西和玛丽·雪莱带着克莱尔和阿莱格拉出发前往意大利，准备按照约定把阿莱格拉交给拜伦时，

sentences.en: He's travelled through Northern Italy and he has ended up in Venice.
sentences.zh: 此时，拜伦已经在威尼斯断断续续地定居了一年多。

sentences.en: And Allegra is a Venetian name.
sentences.zh: 基本上，威尼斯成了他的“主场”，就像希腊曾经是他的主场一样，因为它有一种相似的浪漫色彩。

sentences.en: And by the time that Percy and Mary Shelley, accompanied by Claire and Allegra, set out for Italy to hand over Allegra to Byron, which is what has been agreed.
sentences.zh: 所以他在《恰尔德·哈罗德游记》中写到了这一点，他还在继续写这部作品。

sentences.en: By this point, Byron has been settled in Venice on and off for over a year.
sentences.zh: “我从少年时代就爱上了她。”

sentences.en: And it's basically, it's his kind of place rather in the way that Greece was his kind of place, because it has a similar kind of romance.
sentences.zh: “她对我而言，是一座心中的童话之城，像水柱般从海中升起，是欢乐的居所，是财富的集市。”

sentences.en: So he writes about this in Childe Harold, which he's continuing.
sentences.zh: 但正如希腊处于土耳其统治之下一样，拿破仑战争后的威尼斯也处于奥地利统治之下。

sentences.en: I loved her from my boyhood.
sentences.zh: 所以威尼斯曾经是一个自由共和国，一个大国，但她的独立被拿破仑扼杀了。

sentences.zh: 然后是在更轻快、更有趣的诗歌中，这些诗歌生动地展现了在威尼斯乘贡多拉、住在运河边宫殿里的感觉是多么美妙，就像拜伦所做的那样。

sentences.en: There is a sense now, perhaps for the first time, that Byron is beginning to, dare I say, grow up a bit and calm down.
sentences.zh: 现在有一种感觉，也许是第一次，拜伦开始——我敢说——变得成熟一点，冷静下来了。

sentences.en: He has moved from the city he called Sea Sodom, Venice,
sentences.zh: 他已经从他称之为“罪恶之海”的威尼斯搬到了拉文纳，

sentences.en: to Ravenna, which is even more decayed and dilapidated and faded.
sentences.zh: 那里的衰败、破旧和凋零程度更甚。

sentences.en: And actually, I mean, Ravenna is very nice mosaics, but it's kind of provincial.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我的意思是，拉文纳的马赛克非常漂亮，但它有点偏远。

sentences.en: And that's the one thing Byron has always hated.
sentences.zh: 而那正是拜伦一直讨厌的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's odd.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这很奇怪。

sentences.en: And people who come to visit Byron in Ravenna say, you know, why have you come here?
sentences.zh: 那些去拉文纳拜访拜伦的人会说，你知道，你为什么要来这里？

sentences.en: It's not your kind of place at all.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是你待的地方。

sentences.en: And the reason is that he has fallen for a woman who will be his last and most enduring love.
sentences.zh: 原因是他爱上了一个女人，她将成为他最后也是最持久的爱人。

sentences.en: And she's a 19-year-old Italian contessa, Teresa Guccioli.
sentences.zh: 她是一位19岁的意大利伯爵夫人，特蕾莎·圭乔利。

sentences.en: And she and her husband, and inevitably there is a husband, have their palazzo in Ravenna.
sentences.zh: 她和她的丈夫——不可避免地，她确实有个丈夫——在拉文纳有他们的宫殿。

sentences.en: So Benita Eisler, in her biography of Byron, describes Teresa as a romantic realist, shrewd more than intelligent, innocent and amoral,
sentences.zh: 所以贝妮塔·艾斯勒在她的拜伦传记中，将特蕾莎描述为一位浪漫的现实主义者，精明多于聪明，天真而又非道德，

sentences.en: affected and feeling, worldly and provincial.
sentences.zh: 矫揉造作又多愁善感，世故又乡土气。

sentences.en: I mean, those are a lot of just opposed categories.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些都是许多相互矛盾的范畴。

sentences.en: It's hard to know what that means.
sentences.zh: 很难理解这意味着什么。

sentences.en: Well, Benita Eisler also says that she's simultaneously highly intelligent and utterly frivolous.
sentences.zh: 嗯，贝妮塔·艾斯勒也说她既非常聪明又极其轻浮。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Once blonde and brunette, tall and short.
sentences.zh: 既是金发又是棕发，又高又矮。

sentences.en: No, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 不，我不这么认为。

sentences.en: I mean, I think you can see that they're being very smart, but also being frivolous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为你可以看出他们既非常聪明，又表现得很轻浮。

sentences.en: There is something there that would appeal to Byron, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想那里有一些东西会吸引拜伦。

sentences.en: Yeah, I can see that.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我能看出来。

sentences.en: But also what she gives to Byron is also what Augusta had given Byron, which is a kind of complete and unwavering devotion.
sentences.zh: 但她给予拜伦的，也是奥古斯塔曾经给予拜伦的，那就是一种完全且坚定不移的奉献。

sentences.en: And it's important to say that by this point,
sentences.zh: 而且必须说明的是，到了这个时候，

sentences.en: Augusta is no longer communicating with Byron in the kind of intimate and personal ways that she had previously done, because Lady Byron is still very much on the scene
sentences.zh: 奥古斯塔不再以她之前那种亲密和私人的方式与拜伦交流了，因为拜伦夫人仍然在场，

sentences.en: and has set it as one of her missions to try and redeem Augusta from her sinful state.
sentences.zh: 并将拯救奥古斯塔脱离罪恶状态作为她的使命之一。

sentences.en: So Lady Byron has been born again.
sentences.zh: 所以拜伦夫人已经重生了。

sentences.en: She's become part of the evangelical sect that surrounds William Wilberforce, the great anti-slavery campaigner.
sentences.zh: 她成为了围绕在伟大的反奴隶制运动家威廉·威尔伯福斯身边的福音派教派的一员。

sentences.en: Lady Byron is a committed anti-slavery campaigner.
sentences.zh: 拜伦夫人是一位坚定的反奴隶制运动家。

sentences.en: She is committed to improving the education of the poor, all these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 她致力于改善穷人的教育，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: But among her moral missions is the urge to redeem Augusta.
sentences.zh: 但在她的道德使命中，还有拯救奥古斯塔的冲动。

sentences.en: And so as a result of that,
sentences.zh: 所以结果就是，

sentences.en: Byron is always bewildered by these very stiff letters that he's starting to get from his sister, in which basically she doesn't tell him anything.
sentences.zh: 拜伦总是对他姐姐寄来的那些非常生硬的信感到困惑，信里基本上什么都没告诉他。

sentences.en: And so I think for that reason, he's very susceptible to an Augusta-like figure, which is clearly what Teresa is.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为出于这个原因，他非常容易受到像奥古斯塔那样的人的影响，而特蕾莎显然就是这样的人。

sentences.en: And he stays with her for the rest of his life.
sentences.zh: 他余生都和她在一起。

sentences.en: And it's as close to a monogamous relationship as he will ever know.
sentences.zh: 这是他所能知道的最接近一夫一妻制的关系了。

sentences.en: But it is, of course, a very Byronic form of monogamy in all kinds of ways.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这在各方面都是一种非常“拜伦式”的一夫一妻制。

sentences.en: So Teresa signals her willingness to have him as a lover by Caroline Lamb style, sending Byron a clipping of her pubic hair.
sentences.zh: 所以特蕾莎通过卡罗琳·兰姆的方式，给拜伦寄去了一撮她的阴毛，以此示意她愿意做他的情人。

sentences.en: So my question here is, is this a common practice in the early 19th century?
sentences.zh: 所以我这里的问题是，这在19世纪初是一种常见的做法吗？

sentences.en: Seems to be.
sentences.zh: 似乎是这样。

sentences.en: Or is she deliberately copying Caroline Lamb?
sentences.zh: 还是她在故意模仿卡罗琳·兰姆？

sentences.en: Has she heard about it?
sentences.zh: 她听说过这件事吗？

sentences.en: Probably the latter, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想大概是后者。

sentences.en: Yeah, because people aren't doing this in Jane Austen, right?
sentences.zh: 是啊，因为在简·奥斯汀的小说里人们可不会这么做，对吧？

sentences.en: No, I'm just going to send Mr. Wickham, you know, whatever.
sentences.zh: 不，我只是要寄给威克姆先生，你知道，随便什么东西。

sentences.en: I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我不这么认为。

sentences.en: So there's that.
sentences.zh: 情况就是这样。

sentences.en: There's also the freesome of danger, because her husband, who is 70.
sentences.zh: 此外还有危险的自由，因为她的丈夫已经70岁了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, you know, Teresa is late teens.
sentences.zh: 你知道，特蕾莎才十几岁。

sentences.en: Husband is 70.
sentences.zh: 丈夫70岁。

sentences.en: He's done well for himself.
sentences.zh: 他很有本事。

sentences.en: He's a very powerful figure.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常有权势的人物。

sentences.en: He's a kind of diplomat who's managed to get on well both with Napoleon and the Pope, which is impressive.
sentences.zh: 他是一位外交官，竟然能同时与拿破仑和教皇相处融洽，这令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's believed with some credibility to have murdered people who got in his way, including a previous wife.
sentences.zh: 人们有充分的理由相信，他曾谋杀过阻碍他的人，包括他的一任前妻。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: She has not done well for herself.
sentences.zh: 她可没什么好下场。

sentences.en: But he's very rich.
sentences.zh: 但他非常有钱。

sentences.en: And although she comes from an aristocratic family,
sentences.zh: 虽然她出身贵族家庭，

sentences.en: Count Guccioli, he's a significant figure in Italian politics.
sentences.zh: 古乔利伯爵，他是意大利政坛的重要人物。

sentences.en: So she has done very well for herself.
sentences.zh: 所以她过得相当不错。

sentences.en: And basically, she wants to have her cake and eat it.
sentences.zh: 基本上，她想鱼与熊掌兼得。

sentences.en: So she wants her, you know, all the status and prestige that she gets from being married to this very significant player in Italian politics.
sentences.zh: 她想要，你知道，作为这位意大利政坛重量级人物的妻子所能获得的所有地位和声望。

sentences.en: But she also wants her famous English poet.
sentences.zh: 但她也想要她那位著名的英国诗人。

sentences.en: They also kind of settled down in the palazzo in a weird menage a trois with Dominic shaking his head.
sentences.zh: 他们还在宫殿里安顿下来，形成了一种奇怪的三人行，多米尼克听了直摇头。

sentences.en: It's a bit Nelson and the Hamiltons.
sentences.zh: 这有点像纳尔逊和汉密尔顿夫妇那档子事。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: And I think that it's, that's not a coincidence because this is kind of more accepted in Italy than anywhere else.
sentences.zh: 我认为这并非巧合，因为这种关系在意大利比在其他任何地方都更被接受。

sentences.en: There's this kind of cavalieri servente, this idea that a wife can have a kind of aristocratic, attentive servant.
sentences.zh: 有一种所谓的“骑士侍从”，即妻子可以拥有一位贵族式的、体贴的随从。

sentences.en: Companion.
sentences.zh: 伴侣。

sentences.en: Companion.
sentences.zh: 伴侣。

sentences.en: So this is what happens.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: And I think that Byron's willingness to settle down is enhanced by his feeling that his links to England are being loSt.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，拜伦之所以愿意安顿下来，是因为他感到自己与英国的联系正在丧失。

sentences.en: So not only is Augusta not really writing to him anymore,
sentences.zh: 不仅奥古斯塔不再真正给他写信了，

sentences.en: Lady Melbourne has died.
sentences.zh: 墨尔本夫人也去世了。

sentences.en: So he's lost the spider.
sentences.zh: 所以他失去了那个“蜘蛛”。

sentences.en: That contact as well.
sentences.zh: 那条联系也断了。

sentences.en: And I think also his relations with people back in England is not helped by the fact that this is the period where he begins his greatest poem, Don Juan,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，他与英国人的关系也因为这段时期而变得更糟，因为他开始创作他最伟大的诗作《唐璜》，

sentences.en: which I know people these days tend not to curl up with a kind of massive epic poem.
sentences.zh: 我知道现在的人们往往不喜欢蜷在沙发上读那种宏大的史诗长诗。

sentences.en: But if you curled up with Don Juan, you would be reading the most readable long poem in the whole of English.
sentences.zh: 但如果你读了《唐璜》，你会发现它是整个英语文学中最易读的长诗。

sentences.en: It's like a kind of 18th century novel in verse.
sentences.zh: 它就像一部18世纪的诗体小说。

sentences.en: So it describes Don Juan.
sentences.zh: 它描述了唐璜。

sentences.en: Byron calls him Don Juan for the rhythm and because it's funny.
sentences.zh: 拜伦叫他唐璜是为了韵律，也因为它很有趣。

sentences.en: Don Juan's mother is a scarcely veiled portrait of Lady Byron.
sentences.zh: 唐璜的母亲几乎就是拜伦夫人的写照。

sentences.en: So he mocks both the process of their separation.
sentences.zh: 所以他嘲讽了他们分居的整个过程。

sentences.en: So people who listened to the previous episode may remember Lady Byron rummaging around in his trunks and finding opium and a copy of the Marquis de Sade.
sentences.zh: 听过上一集的朋友可能还记得，拜伦夫人翻遍了他的行李箱，发现了鸦片和一本《萨德侯爵文集》。

sentences.en: So in Don Juan, Juan's mother is called Inez.
sentences.zh: 在《唐璜》中，璜的母亲叫伊内兹。

sentences.en: For Inez called some druggists and physicians and tried to prove her loving lord was mad.
sentences.zh: 因为伊内兹叫来了一些药剂师和医生，试图证明她那可爱的丈夫疯了。

sentences.en: But as he had some lucid intermissions, she next decided he was only bad.
sentences.zh: 但由于他偶尔还有清醒的时候，她接下来决定他只是个坏人。

sentences.en: So that's clearly a portrait of the whole scandal.
sentences.zh: 这显然是对整个丑闻的写照。

sentences.en: And he mocks her by being a brain box, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他嘲讽她是个书呆子，不是吗？

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: A notorious couplet.
sentences.zh: 那句臭名昭著的对联。

sentences.en: But oh, ye lords of ladies intellectual, inform us truly, have they not hen pecked you all?
sentences.zh: “噢，你们这些知识女性的领主们，请如实告诉我们，她们难道没有把你们都管得服服帖帖吗？”

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: One for our feminist listeners to get cross about there.
sentences.zh: 这句足以让我们的女性主义听众感到愤怒了。

sentences.en: I mean, his attitude to women, is he contemptuous women?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他对待女性的态度，他是蔑视女性吗？

sentences.en: He has a misogynist strain, but he adores them as well.
sentences.zh: 他有厌女的一面，但他同时也崇拜她们。

sentences.en: I mean, you're complaining that the description of Teresa is conflicted.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你在抱怨对特蕾莎的描述是矛盾的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, okay.
sentences.zh: 我是说，好吧。

sentences.en: I can understand that he has a complicated relationship with women.
sentences.zh: 我能理解他与女性的关系很复杂。

sentences.en: He has a complicated relationship with women, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为他与女性的关系确实很复杂。

sentences.en: And predictably, when Byron's friends get these, the beginning of Don Juan, they're appalled by it.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，当拜伦的朋友们看到《唐璜》的开头时，他们感到震惊。

sentences.en: And Murray, his publisher, is terrified of publishing it.
sentences.zh: 他的出版商默里被吓坏了，不敢出版它。

sentences.en: And when he does so, eventually he does it without Byron's name on the cover.
sentences.zh: 当他最终出版时，封面甚至没有署拜伦的名字。

sentences.en: But of course, people have only to read it to know that it's Byron.
sentences.zh: 但当然，人们只要一读就知道是拜伦写的。

sentences.en: And so it just adds more to Byron's sulfurous reputation in England.
sentences.zh: 这只会让拜伦在英国那恶名昭彰的声誉雪上加霜。

sentences.en: And I think Byron is quite pleased about this because, you know, on the Oscar Wilde principle, that if there's one thing worse than being talked about, it's not being talked about.
sentences.zh: 我认为拜伦对此相当高兴，因为你知道，按照奥斯卡·王尔德的原则，世界上只有一件事比被人议论更糟糕，那就是没人议论你。

sentences.en: And I think he feels it gives him at least a kind of a hint of the glamour, the Napoleonic glamour that he'd always dreamed of.
sentences.zh: 我认为他觉得这至少给了他一种魅力，一种他一直梦寐以求的拿破仑式的魅力。

sentences.en: And this sense that he is slightly mouldering as an expat, I think he's regretting his exile by this point, is sharpened for him by the events that are happening in England.
sentences.zh: 而这种作为侨民正在逐渐腐朽的感觉，我认为他此时已经后悔流亡了，这种感觉被英国发生的事件所加剧。

sentences.en: Because 1819, of course, is the year of Peterloo, the Peterloo Massacre.
sentences.zh: 因为1819年，当然是彼得卢的一年，彼得卢屠杀。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When strikers are ridden down by the local dragoons.
sentences.zh: 当时罢工者被当地龙骑兵驱赶践踏。

sentences.en: And it gets Shelley very upset.
sentences.zh: 这让雪莱非常难过。

sentences.en: He writes The Mask of Anarchy about it.
sentences.zh: 他为此写了《无政府状态的面具》。

sentences.en: And also it gets John Cam, Hobhouse, Byron's oldest friend, very upset because Hobhouse by this point has become, rather to Byron's surprise,
sentences.zh: 这也让拜伦的老朋友约翰·卡姆·霍布豪斯非常难过，因为霍布豪斯此时已经，令拜伦相当惊讶，

sentences.en: and I think annoyance, a kind of a radical firebrand.
sentences.zh: 我想还有恼火，变成了一个激进的煽动者。

sentences.en: And in December 1819, Hobhouse is sent to Newgate Jail because he's published an incendiary pamphlet and is enshrined as a martyr for liberty among radicals.
sentences.zh: 1819年12月，霍布豪斯被送进了纽盖特监狱，因为他发表了一份煽动性的小册子，并被激进派奉为自由的烈士。

sentences.en: And I think Byron is really jealous.
sentences.zh: 我觉得拜伦真的很嫉妒。

sentences.en: He's quite unpleasant about it, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他对此表现得相当刻薄。

sentences.en: Yeah, he doesn't think that his boring friend, his sidekick, is getting all the attention as the radical martyr.
sentences.zh: 是的，他不认为他那个无聊的朋友、他的跟班能获得作为激进烈士的所有关注。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's like Sherlock Holmes being resentful of Dr. Watson solving a brilliant case.
sentences.zh: 就像夏洛克·福尔摩斯嫉妒华生医生破获了一个精彩的案件一样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 就是那种感觉。

sentences.en: And so whether coincidentally or not, from this point on, he starts to become much more politically involved in British politics, but also in Italian politics.
sentences.zh: 所以无论是否巧合，从那时起，他开始更多地参与英国政治，也参与意大利政治。

sentences.en: And this is partly prompted by the fact that in July 1820, the Pope grants a degree of separation to Count Guiccioli.
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为1820年7月，教皇批准了古乔利伯爵的分居申请。

sentences.en: So he and Teresa separate.
sentences.zh: 所以他和特蕾莎分开了。

sentences.en: And Teresa moves back to live with her father,
sentences.zh: 特蕾莎搬回去和她父亲住在一起，

sentences.en: Count Gamba, he's called.
sentences.zh: 名叫甘巴伯爵。

sentences.en: And Count Gamba is passionately committed to the cause of freeing Italy from Austrian rule and joining up all the disparate parts into which Italy is divided.
sentences.zh: 甘巴伯爵热衷于将意大利从奥地利的统治下解放出来，并将意大利分裂的各个部分统一起来。

sentences.en: And Byron goes with Teresa and so sets up shop with Count Gamba.
sentences.zh: 拜伦跟随特蕾莎，于是和甘巴伯爵一起安顿下来。

sentences.en: And Count Gamba and his son Pietro are part of this kind of secret society that is committed to Italian liberty, the Carbonari.
sentences.zh: 甘巴伯爵和他的儿子彼得罗是致力于意大利自由的秘密组织“烧炭党”的成员。

sentences.en: And early in 1823, there's an abortive revolution in which the Carbonari evolved.
sentences.zh: 1823年初，发生了一场烧炭党参与的流产革命。

sentences.en: Byron is involved very, very tangentially.
sentences.zh: 拜伦参与得非常非常浅。

sentences.en: The revolution fails.
sentences.zh: 革命失败了。

sentences.en: And as a result of this, the Gambas are sent into exile.
sentences.zh: 结果，甘巴一家被流放。

sentences.en: And again, Byron goes with them and he has to leave Ravenna.
sentences.zh: 拜伦再次跟随他们，不得不离开拉文纳。

sentences.en: And he leaves Allegra behind in a convent.
sentences.zh: 他把阿莱格拉留在了修道院。

sentences.en: He's decided that he wants Allegra brought up as a Catholic.
sentences.zh: 他决定让阿莱格拉接受天主教教育。

sentences.en: Byron then heads off to Pisa, which is in Tuscany with its leaning tower.
sentences.zh: 随后拜伦前往比萨，也就是那个有斜塔的托斯卡纳城市。

sentences.en: And there he is joined again by the Shelleys, who've been in Italy all this time.
sentences.zh: 在那里，一直待在意大利的雪莱夫妇再次与他会合。

sentences.en: And when Shelleys meets Byron this time, he's relieved to find that, you know, Byron is no longer fat and bloated and dissipated, but seems much more committed
sentences.zh: 当雪莱这次见到拜伦时，他感到欣慰，因为拜伦不再肥胖、臃肿和放荡，而是显得更加投入，

sentences.en: both to poetry and to politics.
sentences.zh: 无论是对诗歌还是政治。

sentences.en: And again, this kind of paradox, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 又是这种悖论，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Shelleys is simultaneously relieved by this, full of admiration for Byron, but also full of a resentment that almost, I think, borders on hatred.
sentences.zh: 雪莱对此感到欣慰，对拜伦充满钦佩，但同时也充满了几乎接近仇恨的怨恨。

sentences.en: And so Shelleys writes of Byron, I despair of rivaling him as well as I may, and there is no other with whom it is worth contending.
sentences.zh: 于是雪莱写道：“我绝望于能与他匹敌，也没有其他人值得与之竞争。”

sentences.en: But the two poets, they team up, the various other English radicals come out to join them, and they produce a newspaper called The Liberal, which is to be published in England.
sentences.zh: 但两位诗人联手了，其他几位英国激进派也加入了他们，他们创办了一份名为《自由派》的报纸，准备在英国出版。

sentences.en: And the first edition includes a brilliant satire by Byron on the recent death of George III, which is so rude that it gets the guy back in England who has published it.
sentences.zh: 第一期包括拜伦对乔治三世近期去世的一篇精彩讽刺文章，文章内容太粗鲁，导致在英国负责出版的人被起诉。

sentences.en: He goes on trial.
sentences.zh: 他被送上法庭。

sentences.en: Byron has to kind of, you know, keep him in jail when he gets sentenced.
sentences.zh: 拜伦不得不，你知道，在他被判刑时还要供养他。

sentences.en: Byron is back on the public stage in England, not just as a figure of kind of satanic notoriety, but now as a figure of political notoriety.
sentences.zh: 拜伦重返英国公众舞台，不仅作为一个撒旦般的恶名人物，现在更作为一个政治上的恶名人物。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So this is all seems to be kicking off, but then two disasters.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切似乎都要开始了，但随后发生了两场灾难。

sentences.en: The first is that news reaches Byron,
sentences.zh: 第一场是拜伦、

sentences.en: Shelly, Mary Shelly, and in due course, Claire Claremont, that Allegra has died in her convent very young.
sentences.zh: 雪莱、玛丽·雪莱，以及后来的克莱尔·克莱蒙特收到消息，阿莱格拉在修道院年纪轻轻就去世了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: So very tragic.
sentences.zh: 太悲惨了。

sentences.en: Byron has lost his, you know, his second daughter.
sentences.zh: 拜伦失去了他的，你知道，他的第二个女儿。

sentences.en: And then Byron, Shelly,
sentences.zh: 然后拜伦、雪莱、

sentences.en: Teresa's brother, Pietro, various other members of their kind of, you know, their radical set.
sentences.zh: 特蕾莎的兄弟彼得罗，以及他们激进圈子的其他成员。

sentences.en: They're embroiled in a brawl with various dragoons outside Pisa.
sentences.zh: 他们在比萨外与几名龙骑兵卷入了一场斗殴。

sentences.en: And by this point, the Tuscan authorities are fed up with them.
sentences.zh: 此时，托斯卡纳当局已经受够了他们。

sentences.en: They get expelled.
sentences.zh: 他们被驱逐了。

sentences.en: So May 1822,
sentences.zh: 所以1822年5月，

sentences.en: Byron is on the road again.
sentences.zh: 拜伦又踏上了旅程。

sentences.en: And he goes to Livorno, what the English call Leghorn.
sentences.zh: 他去了利沃诺，英国人称之为莱格霍恩。

sentences.en: And he rents a villa there with views over the sea.
sentences.zh: 他在那里租了一栋可以看到海景的别墅。

sentences.en: And Byron always loves the sea.
sentences.zh: 拜伦一直热爱大海。

sentences.en: It always makes him happy because of course, you know, he is lame, but the sea provides him with opportunities to swim.
sentences.zh: 大海总是让他快乐，因为当然，你知道，他跛脚，但大海为他提供了游泳的机会。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: In the sea, Byron is mobile.
sentences.zh: 在大海里，拜伦是行动自如的。

sentences.en: He's a very strong swimmer.
sentences.zh: 他是个非常强壮的游泳者。

sentences.en: Unlike Shelly, of course, who cannot swim.
sentences.zh: 不像雪莱，当然，他不会游泳。

sentences.en: And he and Shelly had both a few months earlier commissioned boats.
sentences.zh: 几个月前，他和雪莱都订购了船只。

sentences.en: So Byron had commissioned a three-masted kind of sailing ship, which he called the Bolivar Dominic.
sentences.zh: 拜伦订购了一艘三桅帆船，他称之为“玻利瓦尔号”，多米尼克。

sentences.en: And I know you love a South American hero of liberation, don't you?
sentences.zh: 我知道你喜欢南美的解放英雄，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, Simon Bolivar.
sentences.zh: 是的，西蒙·玻利瓦尔。

sentences.en: Byron, I think at this point, is seriously thinking maybe of going to South America.
sentences.zh: 我认为拜伦此时正在认真考虑去南美。

sentences.en: He's kind of enthused by stories of Bolivar or indeed even to North America because at this point, the American Mediterranean fleet sails into Leghorn and they invite Byron down
sentences.zh: 他被玻利瓦尔的故事所鼓舞，甚至考虑去北美，因为此时，美国地中海舰队驶入莱格霍恩，他们邀请拜伦上船，

sentences.en: and they kind of toast him.
sentences.zh: 他们还为他祝酒。

sentences.en: And Byron is incredibly flattered by this.
sentences.zh: 拜伦对此感到受宠若惊。

sentences.en: So he is seriously thinking about going to America.
sentences.zh: 所以他正在认真考虑去美国。

sentences.en: But then disaster.
sentences.zh: 但随后灾难降临了。

sentences.en: So Shelly's boat is called the Ariel, even though, again, kind of playing on Shelly's resentment and a sense of inferiority to Byron.
sentences.zh: 雪莱的船叫“爱丽儿号”，尽管这再次体现了雪莱对拜伦的怨恨和自卑感。

sentences.en: Shelly and Byron had initially bought this together and Byron had asked it to be called the Don Jewin.
sentences.zh: 雪莱和拜伦最初是一起买的，拜伦曾要求把它命名为“唐璜号”。

sentences.en: Oh, to rub it in.
sentences.zh: 噢，这是在伤口上撒盐。

sentences.en: Yeah, it hasn't been painted out.
sentences.zh: 是的，名字还没被涂掉。

sentences.en: So Shelly's boat, you know, it's called the Don Jewin, even though he wants to call it the Ariel.
sentences.zh: 所以雪莱的船，你知道，还是叫“唐璜号”，尽管他想叫它“爱丽儿号”。

sentences.en: Both boats are delivered to the respective owners in June and they use them.
sentences.zh: 两艘船都在六月交付给了各自的主人，他们也使用了它们。

sentences.en: And then on the 13th of July,
sentences.zh: 然后在7月13日，

sentences.en: Teresa and Byron in their house above Leghorn, they hear the kind of the crunching on gravel of the wheels of a carriage and there's knocking at the door and there at the door
sentences.zh: 特蕾莎和拜伦在莱格霍恩上方的房子里，听到马车轮子在碎石路上碾过的嘎吱声，有人敲门，站在门口的

sentences.en: is a pale-faced Mary Shelly, white as marble,
sentences.zh: 是脸色苍白的玛丽·雪莱，白得像大理石一样，

sentences.en: Teresa will later write.
sentences.zh: 特蕾莎后来写道。

sentences.en: And Mary says, have you any news of Shelly?
sentences.zh: 玛丽问：你有没有雪莱的消息？

sentences.en: And she tells Byron that Shelly had gone out on the 8th of July, so that's five days before, on the Ariel and hasn't been seen since.
sentences.zh: 她告诉拜伦，雪莱在7月8日，也就是五天前，乘“爱丽儿号”出海后就再也没人见过他了。

sentences.en: Yeah, five days has been gone.
sentences.zh: 是啊，已经失踪五天了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, to reiterate,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，重申一下，

sentences.en: Shelly doesn't swim.
sentences.zh: 雪莱不会游泳。

sentences.en: And so Byron joins the search, they go up and down the coast and on the 18th of July, so that's 10 days after he'd vanished, the body of Shelly and two people
sentences.zh: 于是拜伦加入了搜寻队伍，他们在海岸线上来回寻找，直到7月18日，也就是他失踪10天后，雪莱和另外两名

sentences.en: who'd been with him on the boat are found.
sentences.zh: 和他同船的人的遗体被发现了。

sentences.en: And Shelly has to be recognised by his clothing because his face has been eaten by crabs.
sentences.zh: 雪莱的脸已经被螃蟹啃食，只能通过他的衣物来辨认身份。

sentences.en: Oh, gosh.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And it's agreed that Shelly, as an atheist, as a pagan, should be cremated on the beach, but it takes them a month to get the permits for this.
sentences.zh: 大家一致认为，作为无神论者和异教徒，雪莱应该在海滩上火化，但他们花了一个月才拿到火化许可。

sentences.en: And so Shelly's body and the bodies of the others are buried in quicklime.
sentences.zh: 所以雪莱和其他人的遗体被埋在了生石灰里。

sentences.en: And permission comes through on the 16th of AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 8月16日，许可终于批下来了。

sentences.en: They go into the quicklime, dig up the various bodies.
sentences.zh: 他们走进生石灰坑，挖出了那些遗体。

sentences.en: They find Shelly's skull.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了雪莱的头骨。

sentences.en: Byron had wanted to keep
sentences.zh: 拜伦本想留着

sentences.en: Shelly's skull as a memento.
sentences.zh: 雪莱的头骨作为纪念品。

sentences.en: Would you keep my skull, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你会留着我的头骨吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think I would.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我会的。

sentences.en: Would you?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Well, I would if it wasn't cracked by a spade in the quicklime in which your skull had been preserved, which is what happens to Shelly's.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果它没有在保存你头骨的生石灰里被铁锹敲碎的话，我会的，而雪莱的头骨就是这样被弄坏的。

sentences.en: So it gets shattered, so Byron decides he won't keep it.
sentences.zh: 所以它碎了，拜伦决定不留了。

sentences.en: And so the whole lot gets burned on the beach and Byron can't bear really to watch it because, of course, you know, the corpse is a horrid kind of green indigo colour.
sentences.zh: 于是所有遗体都在海滩上被火化了，拜伦实在不忍心看，因为你知道，尸体呈现出一种可怕的青靛色。

sentences.en: Shelly's barely recognisable.
sentences.zh: 雪莱几乎已经认不出来了。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're not selling it.
sentences.zh: 是啊，你这描述可真够吓人的。

sentences.en: The flesh, the bones start to turn to ashes and Byron doesn't stay.
sentences.zh: 血肉和骨头开始化为灰烬，拜伦没有留下来。

sentences.en: He goes out, wades out into the sea, swims out to the Bolivar, which is a mile and a half offshore to cleanse himself.
sentences.zh: 他走出去，涉水走进海里，游向离岸一英里半的“玻利瓦尔号”，去洗净自己。

sentences.en: With Shelly's death, the whole kind of circle of radicals that had been gathered around Byron and Shelly starts to split up.
sentences.zh: 随着雪莱的去世，围绕在拜伦和雪莱身边的那个激进分子圈子开始分崩离析。

sentences.en: And Byron feels increasingly isolated, increasingly restive, I think, and increasingly alert to events in Greece.
sentences.zh: 我认为，拜伦感到越来越孤立，越来越焦躁，也越来越关注希腊发生的事件。

sentences.en: Because for two years there, the Greeks have been fighting a war of independence.
sentences.zh: 因为在那里，希腊人已经进行了两年的独立战争。

sentences.en: It had broken out in the Peloponnese, so that's the kind of the southern bit of Greece.
sentences.zh: 战争在伯罗奔尼撒半岛爆发，也就是希腊南部地区。

sentences.en: And Byron becomes increasingly obsessed by it.
sentences.zh: 拜伦对此变得越来越痴迷。

sentences.en: And I think this is partly because the dream of Italian liberty is dead.
sentences.zh: 我想这部分是因为意大利自由的梦想已经破灭了。

sentences.en: I mean, all his attempts to kind of work with that have failed.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他所有为之努力的尝试都失败了。

sentences.en: But also, I think, just because he's bored.
sentences.zh: 但我也觉得，只是因为他太无聊了。

sentences.en: So Pietro Gamba,
sentences.zh: 所以彼得罗·甘巴，

sentences.en: Teresa's brother, who's become very close to Byron by this point, he says of Byron that he often felt the want of some other occupation than that of writing.
sentences.zh: 特蕾莎的弟弟，此时已与拜伦非常亲近，他说拜伦经常感到除了写作之外还需要做点别的事情。

sentences.en: So again, it's that idea that Byron had always had, that writing poetry somehow isn't worthy of him.
sentences.zh: 所以这又回到了拜伦一直以来的那个想法，即写诗似乎配不上他。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, without consulting Byron,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在没有咨询拜伦的情况下，

sentences.en: Hobhouse, who's been released by this point from Newgate and is working with the London Greek Committee, so that's the committee that is kind of raising funds for the Greek rebels
sentences.zh: 此时已从纽盖特监狱获释并与伦敦希腊委员会合作的霍布豪斯——也就是那个为希腊叛军筹集资金的委员会——

sentences.en: back in England.
sentences.zh: 在英国提议，

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He suggests to the London
sentences.zh: 他向伦敦

sentences.en: Greek Committee that they should approach Byron.
sentences.zh: 希腊委员会建议应该联系拜伦。

sentences.en: And they do so.
sentences.zh: 他们确实这么做了。

sentences.en: And Byron is wildly enthusiastic.
sentences.zh: 拜伦表现得非常热心。

sentences.en: So this is the first time, isn't it, Tom, that a foreign insurgency has really seized the imagination of the kind of fashionable elites of Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一次，对吧，汤姆，一场外国叛乱真正抓住了欧洲时尚精英们的想象力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So you know how the people do now.
sentences.zh: 你知道现在的人们是怎么做的。

sentences.en: People get very excited about foreign causes and they go on demonstrations.
sentences.zh: 人们对外国事业感到非常兴奋，还会去参加游行。

sentences.en: Yeah, Ukraine would be the example.
sentences.zh: 是的，乌克兰就是一个例子。

sentences.en: Yeah, Ukraine or whatever it might be.
sentences.zh: 是的，乌克兰或其他什么地方。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But this is the first time really it's happened and become a massive kind of cultural phenomenon, I would say.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这是第一次真正发生这种情况，并成为一种巨大的文化现象。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Byron has caught up in it as well.
sentences.zh: 拜伦也卷入其中。

sentences.en: And so when he gets approached by the London Greek Committee, he decides that he will go to Greece in person, even though Teresa is inconsolable about this
sentences.zh: 所以当伦敦希腊委员会找到他时，他决定亲自前往希腊，尽管特蕾莎为此伤心欲绝，

sentences.en: and says to him as he leaves, I know we shall never see each other again.
sentences.zh: 并在他离开时对他说：“我知道我们再也见不到对方了。”

sentences.en: He feels, you know, at last this is what he's been waiting for.
sentences.zh: 他觉得，你知道，这终于就是他一直在等待的机会。

sentences.en: You know, right from the time he first went to Greece, he has dreamed of playing the part of a Napoleon and to do it in the cause of Greek freedom.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从他第一次去希腊开始，他就梦想着扮演拿破仑的角色，并为希腊的自由而战。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of perfect.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这简直太完美了。

sentences.en: And so his plans for Greece are a mix of the practical.
sentences.zh: 所以他为希腊制定的计划既有务实的一面。

sentences.en: So he orders gunpowder, he liquidates as many assets as you can in England to raise liquid funds, but also, of course, the completely romantic.
sentences.zh: 他订购了火药，尽可能变卖在英国的资产以筹集流动资金，但当然，也有完全浪漫的一面。

sentences.en: So inevitably he buys himself
sentences.zh: 所以他不可避免地为自己买了

sentences.en: Pietro Gambo,
sentences.zh: 彼得罗·甘巴，

sentences.en: Teresa's sister, he's going to accompany him, various other people, brilliant outfits.
sentences.zh: 特蕾莎的妹妹，她要陪他一起去，还有其他各种人，以及华丽的装备。

sentences.en: So tremendous uniforms, complete with kind of plumed helmets that are decorated with the goddess Athena on the front.
sentences.zh: 非常壮观的制服，配有饰有雅典娜女神头像的羽毛头盔。

sentences.en: So very, very Byron.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常拜伦风格。

sentences.en: And they set out for Greece on the 13th of July, 1823.
sentences.zh: 他们于1823年7月13日出发前往希腊。

sentences.en: And he sails initially to Kefalonia, which is part of the Ionian Islands.
sentences.zh: 他最初航行到凯法利尼亚岛，那是爱奥尼群岛的一部分。

sentences.en: So those islands that are on the west coast of Greece.
sentences.zh: 也就是希腊西海岸的那些岛屿。

sentences.en: And there he plays basically an ambassadorial role.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他基本上扮演了一个大使的角色。

sentences.en: So he is liaising between London and the rebels who are holed up in a town called Misalonghi, which is kind of set amid lagoons on mainland Greece and which Byron and Hobhouse
sentences.zh: 他在伦敦和躲在迈索隆吉镇的叛军之间进行联络，那个镇坐落在希腊大陆的泻湖之中，拜伦和霍布豪斯

sentences.en: had passed by ship on their original trip.
sentences.zh: 在他们最初的旅行中曾乘船经过那里。

sentences.en: It's not far from Patras, is it?
sentences.zh: 离帕特雷不远，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's also liaising between the Greeks and London with the British military representative there, who is a guy called Napier, who in due course will go on to conquer
sentences.zh: 他还负责在希腊人和伦敦之间与那里的英国军事代表进行联络，那个人叫纳皮尔，后来他征服了

sentences.en: Sindh in India and make the famous pun,
sentences.zh: 印度的信德省，并说了那句著名的双关语，

sentences.en: Bakavi, I have sinned.
sentences.zh: “我犯罪了（I have sinned）”。

sentences.en: And he has a statue in Trafalgar Square.
sentences.zh: 他在特拉法加广场还有一座雕像。

sentences.en: Trafalgar Square.
sentences.zh: 特拉法加广场。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Napier, like Byron, is very, very Phil Hellenic, but is not a free agent in the way that Byron is because he's under
sentences.zh: 纳皮尔和拜伦一样，非常非常亲希腊，但他不像拜伦那样是个自由人，因为他受

sentences.en: British military authority and Britain ostensibly is neutral in the conflict.
sentences.zh: 英国军事当局管辖，而英国表面上在冲突中保持中立。

sentences.en: But Byron absolutely isn't.
sentences.zh: 但拜伦绝对不是。

sentences.en: He continues to try and raise as much money as he can.
sentences.zh: 他继续努力筹集尽可能多的钱。

sentences.en: So we mentioned ages back, it seems now, that Byron's own various coal mines around Rochdale and that the Wicked Lord had rented them out.
sentences.zh: 我们很久以前提到过，拜伦在罗奇代尔周围的各种煤矿，那是邪恶勋爵租出去的。
